# Phase Two — Improved Execution Plan

The Awtsmoos reveals greater light by choosing the vessel that already fits;
Awtsmoos.com grows faster when evidence removes duplication before a single source file shifts.

## Evidence absorbed

- The Apps hub already has a modular catalog, renderer, abortable runtime, and import-only stylesheet manifest.
- `apps/styles/base.css` contains a naked `body` selector.
- `filter.css`, `interactions.css`, `cards.css`, `hero.css`, `discovery.css`, and `responsive.css` use Apps-specific classes without the route root, so their ownership is conventional rather than enforced.
- Card hover is currently unconditional, while filter hover is correctly pointer-qualified.
- Animator is actively being redesigned by a separate same-minute mission with its own final file plan. Those files are reserved from this wave.
- Prior mobile work already verified several high-risk surfaces; this wave must extend evidence instead of rewriting verified pages blindly.

## Wave A — Apps route style isolation

Read every Apps stylesheet completely, then fully rewrite each affected stylesheet so every effective selector is rooted beneath `body[data-geelooy-route="apps"]`.

Preserve the existing variables and visual language. Improve only ownership, interaction modality, containment, and state completeness where evidence supports it.

Candidate full-file rewrites after all reads:
- `geelooy/apps/styles/base.css`
- `geelooy/apps/styles/filter.css`
- `geelooy/apps/styles/interactions.css`
- `geelooy/apps/styles/cards.css`
- `geelooy/apps/styles/hero.css`
- `geelooy/apps/styles/discovery.css`
- `geelooy/apps/styles/responsive.css`

`geelooy/apps/style.css` stays import-only unless a new Apps-local module is justified.

## Wave B — Apps discovery UX

The current runtime is already small, class-based, abortable, and documented. Do not rewrite it merely to satisfy novelty.

Inspect the view and filter policy next. Improve progressive disclosure only if catalog metadata can be surfaced without duplicating the catalog registry. Prefer semantic `<details>` or an Apps-local drawer over permanent dense controls.

## Wave C — Global style-risk evidence

Before touching more pages, locate any existing static-style scanner. If none exists, create one small modular verification tool that reports rather than mutates:
- naked `html`, `body`, `:root`, `*`, and generic element selectors in page-local style families;
- `100vw` and hard viewport widths;
- suspicious fixed/min widths;
- extreme z-index values;
- fixed overlays without containment clues;
- hover-only interactive styles where no focus/active counterpart is visible.

Use its ranked output to choose the next public surfaces. The scanner is evidence generation, not an auto-rewriter.

## Wave D — Agent and docs bridge

Do not duplicate Animator's active agent facade. After its files land, verify them and connect global discovery/docs to the real capability manifest.

Inspect `geelooy/docs`, `geelooy/api`, and `geelooy/.well-known` for the canonical machine-discovery route. Add crosslinks only after the real public contract is known.

## Wave E — Runtime proof

For each changed public surface:
- syntax/static checks;
- selector-scope verification;
- browser console check;
- 320px and 390px overflow probe;
- keyboard focus probe;
- pointer hover/active behavior where relevant;
- reduced-motion check;
- full touched-file reread;
- planned vs actual delta.

## File ownership restraint

This wave will not overwrite Animator files listed in its fresh `04_PHASE_THREE_FINAL_FILE_PLAN.md`, Merkava files in its active same-day mission, or already-verified mobile surfaces unless new evidence proves a regression.
